ai.title: CLI thinking block preview logic
ai.summary: Thinking block preview shows up to 5 lines while streaming, collapses to caret indicator upon completion. Native reasoning blocks hide when message completes via `isMessageComplete` prop. Updates `ThinkingBlock` and `Thinking` components in `cli/src/components/blocks/` and `cli/src/components/`. `PREVIEW_LINE_COUNT` constant increased from 3 to 5.

eli5.text: When the assistant is actively thinking out loud (streaming its reasoning), you'll now see up to 5 lines of that thinking instead of 3. Once the thinking finishes, the preview collapses into a small caret indicator (▸ when closed, ▾ when open) instead of staying expanded. This applies to both regular thinking blocks and native reasoning blocks (which now hide themselves once the full message completes). The change affects anyone watching the CLI output in real-time, making streaming reasoning slightly more visible before it tucks away.

ai.title: Advisory locks replace serializable transactions in credit ops
ai.summary: Billing credit consumption and grants now use `withAdvisoryLockTransaction` instead of `withSerializableTransaction`. This change eliminates serialization failures by making concurrent transactions wait on advisory locks keyed by user/org ID. Affected files include `packages/billing/src/balance-calculator.ts`, `packages/billing/src/grant-credits.ts`, `packages/billing/src/org-billing.ts`, and `packages/internal/src/db/transaction.ts`. New analytics events `ADVISORY_LOCK_CONTENTION` and `TRANSACTION_RETRY_THRESHOLD_EXCEEDED` track lock waits and retry thresholds.

eli5.text: When your account is adding or using credits at the same time as another operation, the system now waits politely for the other one to finish instead of crashing and forcing a retry. This prevents situations where two processes might try to spend the same credits simultaneously, which could leave your balance wrong. The fix applies to credit grants, usage calculations, and organization-level billing, and adds tracking so the team can see when operations are waiting on each other. Everything happens automatically behind the scenes; you wouldn't notice it in your day-to-day usage, but credit operations are now more reliable under busy conditions.

ai.title: Skip advisory lock integration tests in CI without database
ai.summary: advisory-lock.integration.test.ts now skips when CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ACTIONS is true or when DATABASE_URL is missing and RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS is unset. CI injects DATABASE_URL as a secret but provides no running Postgres for packages/internal, causing spurious failures. Change scoped to packages/internal/src/db/__tests__/advisory-lock.integration.test.ts. Billing tests retain their own Postgres service; internal integration tests require explicit opt-in locally.

eli5.text: When you run the project's automated checks on GitHub, the system used to try running database tests even though there was no real database available, which made the checks fail for reasons that had nothing to do with your actual code. Now, those database tests are automatically skipped during automated checks on GitHub, so the checks only fail when something you actually changed breaks them. If you run the same tests on your own computer, they still work the same way as before, unless you explicitly tell them to run the database tests.

eli5.text: The company added a new automated check that runs a set of tests specifically for the billing and credit parts of their internal tools, making sure that recent changes to how credits are handled don't break anything. This is already live and running as part of the company's continuous integration pipeline today.

eli5.text: The help banner that appears at the bottom of your screen when you start a new conversation now shows its keyboard shortcuts and tips in clearly labeled groups instead of one long paragraph. If you look at it, you'll see three sections stacked neatly on top of each other: Shortcuts (like Ctrl+C to stop), Features (like typing @ to mention files), and Credits (explaining how credits work). The credits section also now mentions a new /usage command alongside the existing /buy-credits and /ads:enable commands, giving you another way to check your account balance. This only affects what you see when the help banner pops up the first time, no other part of the app changes.

ai.title: Ctrl+T toggles collapse/expand all in CLI chat
ai.summary: New Ctrl+T keyboard shortcut collapses or expands all collapsible blocks (thinking, agent, tool, agent-list) across all AI responses in the CLI chat view. `handleToggleAll` in `use-chat-messages.ts` calls `setAllBlocksCollapsedState` from new `cli/src/utils/collapse-helpers.ts`, which recursively walks message trees and flips `isCollapsed` on every collapsible block. If any block is expanded, Ctrl+T collapses all; otherwise it expands all. Wired through `keyboard-actions.ts` as a priority-11 action dispatched via `use-chat-keyboard.ts` `onToggleAll`, surfaced in `help-banner.tsx` shortcuts list.

eli5.text: When you're chatting with the AI in the command-line version, you know how sometimes the assistant gives a long answer that's broken into expandable sections (like "thinking", "agent", or "tool" outputs)? Now there's a new keyboard shortcut, just press Ctrl+T, and it will instantly collapse every single one of those sections across your whole chat, or expand them all back open if they're already collapsed. You'd notice this because the help menu at the top of the chat now lists "Ctrl+T" under shortcuts, and the moment you press it, everything tucks away (or unfolds) without you having to click each section one by one.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI 1.0.594 release ships prior same-day CLI and billing
ai.summary: This release-bump commit increments the Freebuff CLI version from 1.0.593 to 1.0.594 in `cli/release/package.json`, packaging the user-visible improvements that landed earlier in the same-day sequence. Consumers upgrade to Freebuff CLI 1.0.594 to receive the Ctrl+T collapse/expand-all shortcut, the battery-style Claude quota indicator, structured help-banner sections, and the advisory-lock credit consumption model across billing services. No code changes accompany this commit; it carries forward the prior CLI and billing edits via the version metadata.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json hunk bumps the `version` field from 1.0.593 to 1.0.594 (commit 3bd658f0 at 2026-01-23T02:54:52Z, Category: CLI, release-bump with +1/-1 stats).

eli5.text: This update brings a new AI helper called thinker-gpt-5 that tackles really tough problems, plus a smarter status bar that shows your usage like a phone battery instead of confusing numbers. You get a new keyboard shortcut, Ctrl+T, that instantly collapses or expands all the details in your conversation so you can focus on what matters, and the input history now behaves correctly when you switch between different input modes. The team also cleaned up the advertising and billing systems to make them more reliable, fixed how multiline answers display in prompts, improved the loading experience when you first start using the product, and added a new section to the help screen that organizes shortcuts, features, and credits in a cleaner layout. Upgrading gives you a smoother, less cluttered chat experience with fewer interruptions from noisy logs and a brand new AI assistant ready for complex questions.

ai.title: Rename CLI task-complete component to task-completed
ai.summary: Renamed `cli/src/components/tools/task-complete.tsx` to `task-completed.tsx` to match the `task_completed` tool name. Updated `registry.ts` import path. Removed outdated docstring comment.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the CLI's internal labeling was cleaned up so the task-completion confirmation screen uses the correct name that matches the underlying tool. You won't see anything different in your terminal because of it, but the change helps the development team keep the code consistent and easier to maintain. It's a minor housekeeping update with no visible impact on how the tool behaves for users.

ai.title: Fix stale state in multiline-input during IME rapid keystrokes
ai.summary: MultilineInput now reads from synchronous refs for value and cursor position during text insertion. This prevents stale closure errors when IME sends rapid multi-character events, ensuring each keystroke builds on the previous state. Affects `cli/src/components/multiline-input.tsx`. Refs are updated synchronously before `onChange` to bypass React batching delays.

eli5.text: When you type Chinese characters quickly, the text you see on the screen was sometimes missing characters or putting the cursor in the wrong spot because the typing tool kept using an old version of your text. You, as the person typing, would notice characters appearing in the wrong place or the cursor jumping unexpectedly during fast typing. The fix makes the typing tool read the very latest text and cursor position right away before inserting each character, so rapid keystrokes now stack correctly instead of piling onto outdated state.

ai.title: File-picker agents exempt from credit billing
ai.summary: Lightweight utility agents (file-picker, file-picker-max, file-lister) now bypass credit consumption when costs are under 5 credits. New `isFreeAgent` helper in `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts` parses agent IDs to identify free-tier agents, preventing unexpected charges for BYOK users. `web/src/llm-api/helpers.ts` updates `consumeCreditsForMessage` to return the actual billed amount, while `web/src/llm-api/openrouter.ts` overwrites response costs with a fake value derived from billed credits to ensure SDK consistency.

eli5.text: If you use the free file-picking helper tools (the quick utility assistants that grab files for you), you'll no longer get charged credits when their total cost is less than 5 credits. A new check instantly recognizes those lightweight helper agents and skips billing them entirely, so anyone running their own subscription through the system won't see surprise charges for these small tasks. The billing code now reports back exactly how many credits were actually charged, and the pricing data you see stays consistent whether or not you got hit with a bill.

ai.title: Advisory lock health check verifies ownership via pglocks
ai.summary: Advisory lock health check now queries pg_locks to verify specific lock ownership instead of just checking connection liveness. Interval reduced from 30s to 10s to detect lost locks faster. Covers packages/internal/src/db/advisory-lock.ts. Triggers lost callback if lock is no longer held despite active connection.

eli5.text: Your billing and credit operations now check themselves more carefully. Every 10 seconds (down from 30), the system asks the database a direct question: "Do I still actually hold this lock?" rather than just checking if the connection is alive. If the system lost the lock but didn't notice, it now triggers an immediate recovery callback instead of silently continuing with a stale lock. This change is active today for internal operations.
